items.text: The A | B slider's hold menu is the same glass panel as the robot's line-ups, centred above the slider, instead of a half-cut rail strip.
The tempo number sits exactly over the middle of its BPM / TAP label, for two-digit and three-digit tempos alike.
The heads-up display no longer jiggles sideways a few pixels: its scrolling part keeps room for the scrollbar, so the text cannot re-wrap each time the bar appears and disappears.

Tap the tempo on the BPM number: hover the metronome or the number and BPM rolls over to TAP, letter by letter. Tap the number to set the tempo, as with the Tap button. On a touch screen the label flips after your first tap and returns two seconds after the last. On narrow bars the Tap button is gone and the number does its job.
Hold the A | B slider for a menu of how it moves: still, ping-pong, sweep or drift. It is the same animator as in the Habits pane.
The little corner markers sit on the flat side: heads-up markers top left, submenu triangles bottom left. Where that corner is rounded they flip to the other side.
Holding a button and then dragging no longer opens its menu.
Clean screen closes the heads-up display and the capture and export panels, so nothing stays open that you cannot reach without the pointer.
The robot, camera and export buttons carry the corner marker too. The Tap button is gone from the tempo bar.

Sliders in the heads-up panes, flyouts and rows follow the Surface standard: a slim line, a round handle, the readout white at its default and in the accent once changed. A double-tap on a slider or its readout glides it back to its default with a small pulse (Surface Reset).
The vertical slider in a flyout has room at its foot.
The Binaural beat section of the heads-up display wears the same headphones icon as its button, so you can tell where you landed.

Controls that open a heads-up pane when you hold them (sound load, binaural, the crossfader's motion) carry a small triangle in the upper right, the way the rail's lower left triangle marks a submenu.
The flyout of the last button in a group, or one low on the screen (the heads-up button), now rises from the button's own level and opens upward.

A saved look now remembers its binaural beat: on or off, the preset (Delta, Theta, Alpha, Tempo), the level and the source. Applying a look, or a performance movement with a look, sets them. Opening the page still never switches a beat on.

A sixteen-column score now fits the frame on a phone (it ran past the stage and under the side rail). Opening a piece switches the A|B habits sweep (and its roll at each edge) off, so it cannot swing the colours or add scenes to the piece.

Make a piece from your scenes (Performance, at the foot, under Pieces): name it and every scene you have, in order, becomes a performance of movements, the same as an opened piece. It keeps the grids, scale, tempo and the way lines run. Save it in My sets or copy it as text and the scenes travel with it. It needs at least two scenes of the same grid size.
